packages.name: M2.4 Bounds and backpressure
packages.work: Runtime options for per-update size, pending bytes, message queues, gap expansion; visible failure on exhaustion
packages.exit_criteria: Memory stays within budget under a flood test; oversized gap terminates with a protocol error
packages.notes: Existing endpoint charged-byte admission and ordinary/auxiliary request-slot limits have runtime-wide current/high-water and admission/release/rejection observations. Tests cover concurrent quota contention, move/zero-byte/rollback accounting, slot independence and release races, retained callback/receive ownership, and reversible aggregate overflow. Charges include reserved receive capacity and retained scenes and do not measure RSS or establish a global memory bound. Full resource policy, flood/RSS budget qualification and product gates remain open. Reference/native actor fixtures hold queued local host publication with three accepted intents while paced peer updates fill either retained-work count or endpoint charged bytes. They require visible RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, service stream cancellation, zero Update RPCs, suppressed queued publication, exact local IDs/owners/bytes/ordinals and retained peer-prefix recovery, independent-endpoint Ping progress, and zero charged reservations/request slots after owner retirement. A third reference fixture holds the first peer decode while an unpaced bounded burst fills all 32 receive slots and overflows the queue. Service cancellation and a native queued-frame snapshot precede decode release, with no byte-budget rejection. Subsequent draining also reaches retained-work capacity; exact local preservation and the peer prefix remain verified. This qualifies controlled receive-queue overflow as well as paced retained-backlog exhaustion; general unpaced load, USD memory amplification and process RSS flood qualification remain open.

packages.coverage_limit: Four public-plugin writers retain seeded queued work through safe A/B/A rotations and through TCP cuts before service execution or after commit/before response. Explicit handler cancellation distinguishes the actual service outcomes without changing client uncertainty. Each writer exports its failed layer to a fresh .usda with SdfLayer::Export; after every original process exits, the standard-library writer_recovery checker requires each export to equal its frozen host layer, contain every planned local operation, and hold at least the before-cut peer prefix with no unapplied peer value, and requires the service ledger to hold only first writes. Public UPDATE counters and service ledger prohibit resend. Three native file-format sample writers retain 18 original admissions through committed-but-unacknowledged sample/map/erase heads and peer sample edits. Exact wire effects are checked before release; after SdfLayer::Export and producer exit, each exported layer's public fields match that writer's frozen host scene, and reading the exports performs no network work. A bounded cleartext HTTP/2 proxy qualifies CANCEL stream reset on a preserved TCP connection, initial graceful GOAWAY with continued old-read progress and new work/resume on backend B, and after-commit reset retaining/exporting Unknown and Queued work. Peer-cancelled reads use bounded recovery; explicit close/terminal cancellation and mutation uncertainty remain separate. A partial-layer-payload case forwards a complete header and seven-byte chunk, proves transport receipt through DATA counts/PING fencing, then resets and resumes on backend B from the last complete cursor with an original queued edit. The service gate also has an exact-remainder release witness. This does not observe worker-internal partial consumption or interrupt within a gRPC message. Session tests reset an established JoinSession stream using real HTTP/2 CANCEL on its existing TCP connection; bounded recovery preserves unsent FIFO and peer identity without awaiting a grace timer. Repeated pre-Connected cancellation exhausts the three-attempt budget. Explicit Leave/local terminal cancellation remain excluded, and messages remain nondurable with possible replay duplication. General structure/value and mixed safe/uncertain-layer workloads, arbitrary partial-message placement, auth/shutdown combinations, additional HTTP/2 errors/TLS termination, long churn, recovery latency/memory budgets and full qualification remain open.
